slides.title: DexTacWAM: A Visuo-Tactile World-Action Model for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.tldr: VISUO-TACTILE WORLD-ACTION MODEL FOR DEXTEROUS MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: DexTacWAM integrates tactile latents into a video diffusion world model to better capture contact dynamics in dexterous manipulation, significantly outperforming vision-centric baselines.

card.one_liner: DexTacWAM extends pretrained video world models to jointly predict visual and multi-finger tactile contact dynamics.
card.key_idea: A finger- and pose-aware compressor aggregates distributed tactile streams into latents, which are injected into a video diffusion world model for joint visuo-tactile state prediction.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on six contact-rich tasks using a 22-DoF bimanual platform; outperformed RDP (70.6% vs 38.0% avg score) with statistically significant improvements.

slides.title: What is the Better Curriculum: Controller-Shaped Grasping Behavior for Contact Force-Sensitive Manipulation
slides.tldr: TACTILE REFLEX CONTROLLER FOR DATA COLLECTION
slides.highlight: This research utilizes a tactile reflex controller as a teacher during data collection to shape grasping behavior, enabling tactile-free policies to achieve high stability in force-sensitive manipulation.

card.one_liner: Tactile reflex controllers improve fragile-object grasping by shaping demonstrations for tactile-free policy learning.
card.key_idea: A 25Hz tactile reflex controller acts as a collection-time teacher, producing stable, controller-shaped demonstrations that a vision-only student policy learns to reproduce without tactile input.
card.evaluation: Tested on ACT and π0.5 policies using fragile plastic cups; reflex-data policies achieved 95% stability versus 15% for manual-data baselines.
card.limitation: Tactile-free policies cannot handle real-time external disturbances, requiring a decoupled high-rate tactile arbiter for reliable grasp retention.

slides.title: MedVLA: A Hierarchical Vision-Language-Action Framework for Closed-Loop Precision Medical Robot Manipulation
slides.tldr: HIERARCHICAL VLA FRAMEWORK FOR PRECISION MEDICAL ROBOTICS
slides.highlight: MedVLA introduces a hierarchical framework coupling multimodal reasoning with constrained execution, relevant to MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for complex societal-scale impact analysis.

card.one_liner: MedVLA is a hierarchical framework for precision medical robotics using constrained function-level execution for safety.
card.key_idea: Decouples high-level LVLM reasoning (think-answer-function triplets) from low-level execution via a state-based gating module and a multi-agent CoT data generation pipeline.
card.evaluation: Tested on flexible electrode implantation; achieved 95% success rate, significantly outperforming OpenVLA (8%) and π0 (15%) in 100 closed-loop trials.
card.limitation: Evaluated on a single task with internally generated data; gating relies on task-specific rules rather than complex anatomical models.

slides.title: Capability-Aware Arbitration for Semantic Intent-Based Shared Control
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework that balances human intent and robot capability to adapt authority, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on human-AI intent alignment and adaptive coaching.

card.one_liner: A shared-control framework that prevents over-helping by combining semantic intent and VLA execution capability confidence.
card.key_idea: Uses a VLM for semantic intent and a VLA for actions, blending authority via a sigmoid mapping of Bayesian-filtered intent confidence and trajectory-based capability confidence.
card.evaluation: 12 participants performed pick-and-place/stacking tasks (ID/OOD). Sem-Cap achieved 92% success, outperforming manual (83%) and intent-only (44%) baselines in success and friendliness.
card.limitation: Bayesian filtering creates a trade-off between temporal stability and responsiveness to genuine intent changes.

slides.title: TACIT: Tactile Contact Supervision for Spatial Attention in Dexterous Manipulation
slides.tldr: TACTILE CONTACT SUPERVISION FOR SPATIAL ATTENTION
slides.highlight: TACIT uses tactile contact data from teleoperated demonstrations to supervise spatial attention in visuotactile diffusion policies, improving success rates in ball placement and peg insertion tasks.

card.one_liner: TACIT uses tactile contact from demonstrations to supervise spatial attention for improved dexterous robot approach.
card.key_idea: Measured tactile contacts are retrospectively used as Gaussian targets to train a camera-point attention head, which pools spatial features to condition a visuotactile diffusion policy.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on real-robot (ball/peg) and simulated tasks. TACIT achieved 66.7% and 73.3% success in real benchmarks, significantly outperforming vision-only and fusion baselines.
card.limitation: Does not establish semantic object detection and may not generalize beyond the training workspace or to deformable objects.

slides.title: Tactile-JEPA: Topology-Aware Self-Supervised Representation Learning for Distributed Tactile Sensors
slides.highlight: Tactile-JEPA improves force estimation and in-hand orientation by learning topology-aware representations from distributed tactile sensors. This supports MOSAIC's focus on physics and force-based human proficiency estimation.

card.one_liner: Tactile-JEPA uses topology-aware self-supervised pre-training to improve representations for distributed electronic skin sensors.
card.key_idea: Predicts masked taxel embeddings using a connectivity graph to sample dual-scale (local and global) masks, capturing both fine contact details and global surface states.
card.evaluation: Tested on Sparsh-skin, Tactile socks, and DECO-50 datasets; reduced force estimation error by 6.3% and in-hand orientation error by 20.8% over prior SOTA.

slides.title: Norm2Tex: Augmenting Visuo-Tactile Simulations with Texture
slides.highlight: Norm2Tex reduces the domain shift between simulated and real tactile data by integrating high-frequency surface details from normal map textures into simulation pipelines.

card.one_liner: Norm2Tex augments visuo-tactile simulations with high-frequency surface textures to reduce the sim-to-real gap.
card.key_idea: A plug-in method that converts normal maps into pseudo-height maps via Fourier-domain Poisson integration, modifying a simulator's depth map before rendering without altering underlying mesh geometry.
card.evaluation: Tested on TACTO and Taxim simulators; achieved 72% zero-shot material classification accuracy and material-dependent behavior in a RL-based grasp force task.
card.limitation: Does not model deformation-dependent illumination artifacts (e.g., shadows), leading to a remaining sim-to-real gap for smooth materials like acrylic.

slides.title: Dexterous Robot Manipulation from Human Demonstrations via Contact-Anchored Retargeting and Residual Policy Learning
slides.highlight: This work proposes a pipeline to convert human motion-capture into robot policies by focusing on contact structure and using residual RL for physical consistency, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on procedural skill acquisition and ego-exo views.

card.one_liner: A pipeline converting human motion-capture to robot policies using contact-anchored retargeting and residual RL.
card.key_idea: Physics refinement recovers contact forces via residual RL; contact-anchored retargeting transfers contact structures across morphologies; a second residual policy restores dynamic feasibility for robot hardware.
card.evaluation: Tested on 25,454 single-hand and 250 dual-hand trajectories; validated across four distinct robot hands and four real-world bimanual tasks with zero real-robot training.
card.limitation: In-hand reorientation remains challenging (3/10 success) due to compounding timing errors during continuous re-grasping.
